summary: Internet-reachable cloud and cluster resources, over-broad identity and storage policy, and server-side request paths to instance metadata or internal control planes, as declared in IaC and reachable from application code.
looks_for: security groups, firewall rules or NetworkPolicy gaps allowing 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 ingress to admin, database, SSH/RDP or cluster API ports
load balancers, ingresses, Service type LoadBalancer/NodePort or public IPs fronting internal-only or admin services
storage buckets, blobs or snapshots with public ACLs, public-read bucket policies, disabled public-access blocks or anonymous-listable containers
IAM/RBAC policies with wildcard actions or resources, iam:PassRole or sts:AssumeRole to broad principals, cluster-admin bindings, or trust policies open to any account
workload identity that is broader than the workload needs: node or instance roles shared by all pods, automounted service account tokens, IRSA/Workload Identity bound to over-privileged roles
instance metadata left reachable: IMDSv1 allowed (http_tokens optional), hop limit above 1 for containers, no egress block to 169.254.169.254 or metadata.google.internal
server-side fetches of user-controlled URLs (webhooks, image/PDF fetchers, URL previews, import-from-URL, proxy endpoints) with no allow-list or post-DNS-resolution address check
privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID or hostPath-mounting pods, docker.sock mounts, and containers running as root with added capabilities
unauthenticated or anonymous-enabled control planes and dashboards: kubelet, Kubernetes API, etcd, Docker API, Kubernetes dashboard, managed-database public endpoints
unrestricted egress (0.0.0.0/0 egress rules, no egress NetworkPolicy) that turns a foothold into callback or exfiltration
long-lived cloud credentials or tokens in IaC variables, tfvars, Helm values, container env or state files
internet-facing resources absent from the threat model or architecture docs supplied with the target
preconditions: the resource is reachable from the attacker's position: internet-routable address, public DNS, or public endpoint flag set in the deployed configuration
the IaC or manifest path carrying the misconfiguration is the one actually deployed for the environment in scope (not a dev, example or test module)
for SSRF: an unauthenticated or low-privilege request can set the scheme, host or port of a server-side fetch
for metadata access: the fetching workload runs on a cloud instance or node whose metadata service accepts the request (IMDSv1, or IMDSv2 with a hop limit the request can meet)
for identity abuse: the obtained credential or token is bound to a role whose policy grants actions beyond the workload's need
no compensating control on the path: private endpoint, WAF or gateway allow-list, VPC service controls, organization policy or SCP that denies the action
proof_obligations: the exposing resource cited at file:line (Terraform resource, CloudFormation logical id, Kubernetes manifest or Helm value) with the exact attribute that opens it
the scanner result that flags it, by tool and rule id (Checkov, Trivy, KICS), or an explicit statement that no scanner covered the resource
evidence the resource is deployed for the in-scope environment: module call chain, workspace or overlay that includes it, or the variable value that enables it
for SSRF: the user-controlled input at file:line reaching the HTTP client call at file:line with no allow-list, scheme restriction or resolved-address check on the path
for metadata access: the SSRF sink plus the IaC or node config showing IMDSv1 or hop-limit permits the call, and the role attached to that instance or workload
for IAM/RBAC escalation: the policy document or binding at file:line and the concrete action chain it permits (e.g. PassRole plus a compute create action)
the compensating controls that were checked (SCP, org policy, NetworkPolicy, private endpoint, WAF) and where each was found or found absent
false_positive_traps: declared-but-not-deployed exposure: example, test or disabled modules, count = 0, or a variable default overridden to private in the environment's tfvars or overlay
public exposure that is intended and fronted: a CDN or load balancer serving static content, or a public API behind authentication and rate limiting
0.0.0.0/0 on an egress rule, on port 80/443 of a web tier, or on a security group attached to nothing
bucket policies that grant access to a CloudFront origin access identity, VPC endpoint or specific account rather than to everyone
wildcard IAM statements constrained by a Condition block, permission boundary or resource-scoped ARN that the scanner rule does not evaluate
a URL-fetching function whose destination is a constant, config value or allow-listed host the request cannot influence
cluster-admin or privileged workloads that are the platform's own system components (CNI, CSI, ingress controller) installed from a pinned upstream chart
scanner findings on vendored upstream charts or modules that the target overrides with values not visible to the scanner
must_not: report declared IaC exposure as observed runtime exposure; state which it is
probe, scan or fetch any live cloud endpoint, metadata address or account; reason from the target's files and the run's tool evidence only
treat a scanner rule hit as exploitable without the deployment and reachability evidence above
